paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The effect of and by language family. Error bars indicate the standard deviation.
model_annotation: The chart illustrates the “effect” measured for different language families, shown as grouped bars for four model/condition combinations with error bars indicating standard deviation. The horizontal axis contains the language-family categories labeled (from left to right) IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, with no additional axis title shown; the categories appear in this presented order rather than being sorted by bar height. The vertical axis is labeled “effect” and uses a linear numeric scale with labeled ticks at approximately 0, 10, 20, 30, and 40 (values extend slightly above 40 based on the plotted area). Within each family, four adjacent bars are shown in a consistent left-to-right grouping: mBERT-targ (light blue), XLM-targ (dark blue), mBERT-permute (light green), and XLM-permute (dark green). Approximate bar heights by family are: IE-Baltic ~22 (mBERT-targ), ~15 (XLM-targ), ~5 (mBERT-permute), and ~5 (XLM-permute); IE-Germanic ~13, ~12, ~8, and ~9; IE-Indic ~4, ~5, ~18, and ~16; IE-Romance ~15, ~12, ~3, and ~2–3; IE-Slavic ~14, ~11, ~9, and ~8; IE-other ~14, ~11, ~5, and ~5; Isolate ~35, ~25, ~1–2, and ~1–2; Semitic ~10, ~10–11, ~8–9, and ~8–9; and Uralic ~28, ~21, ~1–2, and ~1. Each bar includes a vertical black error bar with caps, with visibly larger spreads for some families (e.g., Isolate and Uralic) and smaller spreads for others (notably the permute bars for Isolate and Uralic); no bars are specially highlighted beyond the legend-based color coding.
